mechanism.name: Conditional mean of the nonlinear AR(1) regression in the Zhao–Wu simultaneous confidence band simulation

generation_equations.label: 1. Initialization
generation_equations.expression: Set Y0=0 and burn_in=1000 before collecting the n regression pairs. Implementation choices; not source-specified initialization or burn-in parameters.

generation_equations.label: 2. Innovation sequence
generation_equations.expression: epsilon_t iid N(0,1), independent of the past; draw sequentially during recursion. Source standard-normal innovations; noise multiplier s=0.4.

generation_equations.label: 3. Recursion
generation_equations.expression: Y_t=0.9*sin(Y_(t-1))+0.4*epsilon_t for burn_in+n updates. Compute source nonlinear mean before adding each independent innovation.

generation_equations.label: 4. Observation pairs
generation_equations.expression: Return (X_i,Y_i)=(Y_(burn_in+i-1),Y_(burn_in+i)), i=1..n. Deterministic export in time order; X_(i+1)=Y_i exactly; no innovation column.

sampling.unit: time series observation (consecutive pairs of one Markov chain realisation)
sampling.dependence: Time-homogeneous Markov recursion with finite zero initialization and burn-in 1000; adjacent pairs share X_(i+1)=Y_i; exact stationarity is not asserted.

assumptions: Time-homogeneous first-order Markov recursion Y_t=.9*sin(Y_(t-1))+.4*epsilon_t; innovations iid N(0,1) and independent of the past.
The mean map is globally contractive with Lipschitz constant .9. The process admits an invariant law, but the finite simulation starts at zero; burn-in 1000 does not certify exact stationarity.
Adjacent exported rows are dependent: X_(i+1)=Y_i. The marginal distribution after finite initialization need not equal the invariant law.
For every exported time, the new innovation has conditional mean zero. Therefore E[Y_t|Y_(t-1)=x]=.9*sin(x) without an exact-stationarity assumption.
The positive Gaussian transition density gives support around each fixed query after at least one update.
No band coverage, finite-sample cutoff, mixing-rate estimate or named human scientific acceptance is established by the diagnostics.

properties.notes: Single scalar covariate X = Y_{i-1}; the regression function mu(x) = 0.9*sin(x) is nonlinear in x. The serial dependence itself comes from the first-order Markov recursion, not from interactions or from extra covariates. No products of covariates are formed. high_dimensional is false: there is exactly one covariate for any sample size.

estimand.name: mu(x0) = E[Y_i | X_i = x0] = 0.9*sin(x0)
estimand.definition: Pointwise conditional mean of the Markov regression at a single fixed query point x0 inside the source design interval T = [-1.1,1.1]; a scalar quantity, not a simultaneous confidence band and not a coverage probability.

truth.expression: Pointwise conditional mean of the Markov regression at a single fixed query point x0 inside the source design interval T = [-1.1,1.1]; a scalar quantity, not a simultaneous confidence band and not a coverage probability.
truth.derivation: Closed form mu(x0) = a*sin(x0) with a = 0.9, evaluated by standard-library math.sin and cross-checked by a numpy evaluation, a 60-digit Decimal Taylor series and a Gauss-Hermite integration of the innovation law; no rows from generate() are used.

adaptations: Keep Model 1 only; Model 2 targets conditional variance rather than the selected mean target.
Set Y0=0 and burn-in=1000 as explicit implementation choices, not recovered paper parameters.
Keep chronological Markov pairs and add fixed query x0=0.5 or 0.0; run CPU pointwise checks instead of the original band experiment.
